# AI Agent Prompt Builder

This example converts a webhook payload into a safe AI-agent prompt.

It is designed for summaries, dashboards, and workflow routing. It does not tell the agent to make trading decisions or invent missing data.

## Run

```bash
node prompt-builder.js ../payloads/confirmed-buys.json
node prompt-builder.js ../payloads/no-picks.json
```

## Use Cases

- daily signal summary
- Discord explanation
- personal watch note
- trade journal draft
- AI agent routing input

Keep broker execution behind separate risk controls and human approval.

# Security and Signing

Webhook signing lets your receiver confirm that a payload came from KamdenAI and was not modified in transit.

## Headers

KamdenAI sends these headers with signed deliveries:

```text
X-KamdenAI-Event
X-KamdenAI-Delivery
X-KamdenAI-Timestamp
X-KamdenAI-Signature
```

## Verification Concept

The exact signing string should match the Developer API documentation inside the product. A common pattern is:

```text
timestamp.rawBody
```

Then compute an HMAC SHA-256 signature using the signing secret.

## Node Example

```js
import crypto from "node:crypto";

function verifySignature({ rawBody, timestamp, signature, secret }) {
  const payload = `${timestamp}.${rawBody}`;
  const expected = crypto
    .createHmac("sha256", secret)
    .update(payload)
    .digest("hex");

  return crypto.timingSafeEqual(
    Buffer.from(signature, "hex"),
    Buffer.from(expected, "hex")
  );
}
```

## Python Example

```python
import hmac
import hashlib

def verify_signature(raw_body: bytes, timestamp: str, signature: str, secret: str) -> bool:
    payload = timestamp.encode("utf-8") + b"." + raw_body
    expected = hmac.new(secret.encode("utf-8"), payload, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(signature, expected)
```

## Replay Protection

Reject old timestamps. A common tolerance is 5 minutes.

## Secret Storage

Store secrets in environment variables:

```text
KAMDENAI_SIGNING_SECRET=whsec_example_do_not_commit
```

Never commit real secrets to GitHub.

# AI Agent Workflows

Signal webhooks can be used as inputs for custom AI agents, Hermes agents, or other agentic workflows.

## Good Agent Use Cases

- Summarize daily signal payloads.
- Convert raw payloads into plain-English alerts.
- Compare today's signals against your journal.
- Prepare a pre-market watch note.
- Route signals into a dashboard.
- Tag signals by sector or risk size.
- Create personal reminders.

## Risky Agent Use Cases

Be careful with:

- fully autonomous live trade execution
- account-level position sizing
- order cancellation logic
- stop movement decisions
- options routing
- margin workflows

Agents can hallucinate, misread fields, or make assumptions. Use guardrails and manual approval.

## Recommended Architecture

```text
KamdenAI webhook
  -> verified receiver
  -> normalized event queue
  -> AI summarizer or agent
  -> human review
  -> optional broker workflow
```

## Agent Prompt Pattern

```text
You are analyzing a stock signal webhook payload.
Summarize the tickers, entry, stop, target, and risk/reward.
Do not invent missing fields.
Do not provide financial advice.
If there are no rows, report that fact without inferring review completion.
Research and preparation are not official signals.
Keep modeled results, afternoon studies, and broker fills separate.
```

# Automation Recipes

These are public-safe ways to build around signal webhooks without exposing private strategy logic.

## Discord Alert Channel

```text
Webhook received
  -> if data.confirmedBuys has rows
  -> format message
  -> post to #confirmed-buys
```

Best for: community alerts, private groups, personal signal rooms.

## Google Sheets Signal Log

```text
Webhook received
  -> choose event rows
  -> for plans use data.scan.buySignals/watchSignals
  -> for buys use data.confirmedBuys
  -> for exits use data.quickExitResults
  -> append row to sheet
  -> include delivery ID
```

Best for: tracking, audits, trade review, no-code history.

## AI Agent Brief

```text
Webhook received
  -> build prompt from payload
  -> ask agent to summarize without financial advice
  -> send summary to email or Discord
```

Best for: plain-English daily summaries, personal prep notes, searchable context.

## Private Dashboard

```text
Webhook received
  -> save raw payload in database
  -> normalize latest signals
  -> frontend reads normalized rows
```

Best for: custom UI, advanced filtering, result review.

## Broker Workflow Helper

```text
Webhook received
  -> verify signature
  -> calculate user sizing
  -> create draft order ticket
  -> require manual approval
```

Best for: experienced builders. Start with paper trading.

## No-Pick Day Logger

```text
Webhook received
  -> if confirmedBuys is empty or noConfirmedBuys is true
  -> log no confirmed rows supplied; inspect review completion
  -> send optional "no picks today" note
```

Best for: tracking delivered empty events separately from incomplete reviews and missing deliveries.

# KamdenAI Signal System & Automation Guide

**Eight ranked candidates. Clear decisions. A plan for every confirmation.**

[Explore KamdenAI membership](https://kamdenai.com) · [Understand the signal system](docs/signal-system.md) · [Build an integration](docs/getting-started.md)

KamdenAI brings opening stock rankings, published signal plans, recorded morning outcomes, and a member workspace into one focused routine. The opening board can confirm several candidates independently. Read each card's status before its rank: eight candidates does not mean eight trades.

This public guide explains the member experience and provides consumer-side webhook examples. All examples use fictional symbols and illustrative prices. The signal engine, selection formulas, weights, qualification thresholds, data-provider configuration, and production infrastructure remain private.

## The current signal workflow

| Stage | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Before the open | Research and preparation provide context. They are not official signals and do not restrict the later opening field. |
| After opening review | Up to eight ranked candidates receive individual decisions. Zero to eight may be Confirmed, each with a published entry, stop, and target. Check the session date and actual publication time. |
| Morning results | The current modeled policy follows target or stop after eligible entry, then a 10:05 AM Eastern reference exit for remaining positions. Processing may finish later. |
| Separate 3 PM study | Hypothetical later holding comparisons and watchlist movement support review. They are excluded from official morning returns. |

Confirmed is an official signal, not a broker fill. Watch only, No buy, and Ungraded candidates are observation or incomplete-review records. Rank one can be Watch only while ranks two and five are Confirmed. No confirmed signals is a valid session outcome.

## Your member workspace

- **Feed → Signals:** opening rankings, individual decisions, published plans, and daily results.
- **Signal Results:** review recorded outcomes, including losses, no fills, and unavailable evidence.
- **Journal:** record your own broker fills, shares, exits, and notes separately from modeled results.
- **Stock News and community:** add context and discussion; member posts do not create official confirmations.
- **Developer webhooks:** route selected events into your own tools where available in your account.

KamdenAI does not place broker orders. Members choose whether to trade and control their own execution, position size, and combined exposure. A signal can lose money, and several confirmed names can lose together.

## Build around the published record

```text
KamdenAI published event
  -> signed webhook
  -> your verified HTTPS receiver
  -> private alerts / Sheets / dashboard / journal / AI summary
```

| Event | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `research_watchlist.created` | Research context, typically around 9:15 AM Eastern; preparation only |
| `morning_scan.created` | Pre-open preparation, typically around 9:28 AM Eastern; not confirmation |
| `confirmed_buys.created` | Official confirmed signals after opening review; iterate every confirmed row |
| `quick_exit_results.created` | Recorded morning outcomes using the 10:05 reference policy |

These are reference stages, not delivery guarantees. Use the actual publication timestamp when present, session date, and completion indicators. An empty array alone does not prove that every candidate was reviewed. Test events verify delivery, not the trading system.

## Start here

1. Read the [Signal System Guide](docs/signal-system.md).
2. Follow [Getting Started](docs/getting-started.md) and [Webhook Events](docs/webhook-events.md).
3. Review [Payload Fields](docs/payload-field-reference.md), [Security and Signing](docs/security-and-signing.md), and [Architecture](docs/architecture.md).
4. Choose an [Automation Recipe](docs/automation-recipes.md).
5. Read [Result Tracking](docs/historical-results.md) and [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md).

Abbreviated sample, not a live signal or a complete schema. Fictional symbol DEMOA is rank two; rank does not determine official status.

```json
  "event": "confirmed_buys.created",
  "dateKey": "2026-10-08",
  "sentAt": "2026-10-08T13:34:10.000Z",
  "data": {
    "publishedAt": "2026-10-08T13:34:05.000Z",
    "confirmedBuys": [{
      "ticker": "DEMOA",
      "entry": 20,
      "stop": 19.5,
      "target": 20.5,
      "openingConfirmation": {
        "officialRank": 2,
        "status": "confirmed_buy",
        "statusLabel": "Confirmed buy"
      }

}
```

[More illustrative payloads](examples/payloads) include multiple confirmations, incomplete decisions, no-confirmation events, and modeled wins and losses. They are shortened teaching examples; check the Developer API documentation and test delivery in your account for available fields.

# Discord Formatter

This example turns a signal payload into a simple Discord-ready message.

## Run

```bash
node format-discord-message.js ../payloads/confirmed-buys.json
node format-discord-message.js ../payloads/no-picks.json
```

Use the output as the message body in Discord, Make.com, Zapier, or your own bot.

# Simple Dashboard

This is a static demo dashboard. It does not receive live webhooks by itself. Paste a sample payload into the textarea to preview how signal data could be displayed.

Open `index.html` in a browser.

For a real dashboard, connect your webhook receiver to a database and have the frontend read normalized events from that database.

# Node Webhook Receiver

Minimal Express receiver for KamdenAI-style signal webhooks.

## Setup

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env
npm start
```

Then expose the local server with an HTTPS tunnel:

```bash
ngrok http 3000
```

Paste the HTTPS forwarding URL plus `/webhook` into your Developer API page.

## Environment

```text
KAMDENAI_SIGNING_SECRET=whsec_example_do_not_commit
PORT=3000
```

## Endpoint

```text
POST /webhook
```

The example logs the event, delivery ID, and signal count.

# Python Webhook Receiver

Minimal Flask receiver for KamdenAI-style signal webhooks.

## Setup

```bash
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
copy .env.example .env
python app.py
```

Use an HTTPS tunnel for local testing, then paste the public URL plus `/webhook` into your Developer API page.

# Google Sheets Logger

This example is a no-code pattern for logging signal events into Google Sheets.

## Sheet Columns

Create a sheet with these columns:

```text
Received At
Date Key
Event
Ticker
Company
Entry
Stop
Target
Risk Per Share
Reward Per Share
Target R
Status
Delivery ID
Message
```

## Make.com Scenario

1. Webhooks: Custom webhook
2. Router:
   - Route A: rows exist for the selected event
   - Route B: no official picks or `data.noConfirmedBuys = true`
3. Route A:
   - Iterator over `data.scan.buySignals[]`, `data.scan.watchSignals[]`, `data.confirmedBuys[]`, or `data.quickExitResults[]`
   - Google Sheets: Add a row
4. Route B:
   - Google Sheets: Add a no-pick row

## Why This Works

You get a full event history, including days where no signals qualified.

# Illustrative Payloads

All symbols, prices, decisions, and results here are fictional. These shortened examples show consumer handling, not a full schema or private engine logic. Check your account's Developer API documentation and test delivery.

- `research-watchlist.json` and `morning-scan.json`: preparation only.
- `confirmed-buys.json`: eight candidate decisions, ranks two and five confirmed, rank seven incomplete. `confirmationComplete: false` does not invalidate the supplied confirmed decisions or qualify the incomplete candidate.
- `no-picks.json`: completed review with no official confirmations.
- `quick-exit-results.json`: modeled target win and stop loss for the same two confirmations; no broker fills and no embedded cost adjustment.
- `historical-results-example.json`: tracking assumptions, not historical performance.
- `webhook-test.json`: delivery test only.

No fills and unavailable results are separate states. Do not invent result values when evidence is missing. Afternoon studies stay separate from morning returns.

# Risk Sizing Calculator

Generic risk sizing example for builders.

This does not include KamdenAI private signal logic. It simply shows how a user could size a position from public fields like entry and stop.

## Run

```bash
node risk-sizing.js --cash=5000 --risk=1 --entry=24.50 --stop=23.95
node risk-sizing.js --cash=10000 --risk=1 --entry=24.50 --stop=23.95
```

## Output

The script prints:

- planned risk dollars
- risk per share

Always verify sizing with your broker and your own risk rules.

# Security

This public repo should never contain production secrets, private keys, paid signal data, Firebase config, webhook signing secrets, or proprietary scan logic.

## If You Find a Secret

If you believe a secret was accidentally committed, immediately rotate the secret in the owning platform and remove it from git history before relying on the new value.

## Webhook Security Basics

- Use HTTPS endpoints only.
- Keep signing secrets private.
- Verify signatures before trusting payloads.
- Reject old timestamps to reduce replay risk.
- Never expose broker API keys in frontend code.
- Use paper trading before any live execution workflow.
- Add manual confirmation for broker-connected automations.
- Log delivery IDs so duplicate events can be ignored.

## Public Repo Boundary

This repo is intentionally limited to consumer-side examples:

- webhook receiver examples
- signature verification examples
- payload formatting examples
- dashboard examples
- automation checklists

It does not include internal signal generation rules or private platform code.

# Troubleshooting

## No rows or no delivery

An empty array supplies no rows for that event. Inspect event type, review completion, and candidate decisions before calling it a completed no-signal session. A test event checks delivery only. No delivery is a separate issue: check the selected events, endpoint, and delivery history.

## Missing or delayed decisions

Check session date, actual publication time, and connection status. Ungraded candidates have incomplete evidence; do not infer confirmation or failure. Valid confirmed candidates can coexist with incomplete candidates.

## Results differ from a broker account

System outcomes use a stated model and evidence. Broker timing, prices, shares, costs, and exits can differ. Record personal execution in Journal. No fill and unavailable results are not completed return observations.

## Duplicate events or signature errors

Store delivery IDs to ignore retries. Verify the original raw body with the signing format documented in your account. Check the timestamp, server clock, and secret without printing credentials in logs. See [Security and Signing](security-and-signing.md).

# Google Sheets Logging

Google Sheets is useful for keeping a clean signal history.

## Suggested Columns

- Date
- Event
- Ticker
- Company
- Entry
- Stop
- Target
- Risk per share
- Reward per share
- Target R
- Status
- Notes
- Delivery ID
- Received at

## Make.com Flow

```text
Webhook trigger -> pick rows by event -> Google Sheets Add Row
```

Use `data.scan.buySignals[]` and `data.scan.watchSignals[]` for the 9:28 plan scan, `data.confirmedBuys[]` for the official opening signals, and `data.quickExitResults[]` for the 10:05 result.

For no-pick days, add a single row with:

- Event
- Date
- Count: 0 or noConfirmedBuys: true
- Message

## Why Log No-Pick Days?

Completed no-confirmation records document an outcome; empty rows alone do not prove review completion. That makes your logs cleaner because you can distinguish "nothing qualified" from "the webhook broke."

## Template

See [examples/google-sheets-logger](../examples/google-sheets-logger).

# Make.com Guide

Make.com is one of the easiest ways to turn signal webhooks into automations without writing code.

## Basic Setup

1. Create a new scenario.
2. Add the Webhooks app.
3. Choose Custom webhook.
4. Create a webhook.
5. Copy the Make webhook URL.
6. Paste it into the KamdenAI Developer API page.
7. Select the events you want.
8. Click Send Test.

If Make shows the test payload, the connection works.

## Common Automations

- Send the 9:28 plan scan, opening confirmations, and 10:05 quick-exit results to Discord.
- Add rows to Google Sheets.
- Send yourself an SMS when `confirmed_buys.created` has picks.
- Create a daily Notion page.
- Feed payloads into an AI summarizer.
- Store all events in Airtable.

## Filter Example

Only continue if a confirmed-buy event has official picks:

```text
length(data.confirmedBuys) > 0
```

Route no-pick days separately:

```text
length(data.confirmedBuys) = 0
```

## Useful Fields

In Make, you can map:

- `event`
- `dateKey`
- `sentAt`
- `data.scan.buySignals[]`
- `data.scan.watchSignals[]`
- `data.confirmedBuys[]`
- `data.quickExitResults[]`
- `data.message`

## Signing Secret

Make can receive the webhook without signature verification, but production workflows should verify signatures if possible.

If you cannot verify signatures inside Make directly, keep the webhook URL private and consider routing through your own small receiver first.

# Broker Automation

You can use signal webhooks as inputs for broker-connected workflows, but this should be handled with extreme care.

## Safer First Steps

Start with:

- alerts
- dashboards
- paper trading
- manual approval buttons
- order ticket prefill
- position sizing calculators

Avoid jumping directly to live automatic execution.

## Suggested Flow

```text
Webhook received
  -> verify signature
  -> validate signal fields
  -> calculate user-specific sizing
  -> show human approval
  -> send order to broker API
  -> log broker response
```

## Broker API Notes

Every broker is different. You need to understand:

- supported order types
- market hours
- extended-hours behavior
- buying power rules
- margin restrictions
- stop order behavior
- rate limits
- API permission scopes
- paper trading availability

## Hard Rule

Never store broker API keys in frontend code or public GitHub repos.

Use backend secrets, least-privilege keys, and paper trading first.

# Launch Checklist

Use this before sharing a webhook integration with other people.

## Public Repo Safety

- [ ] No API keys
- [ ] No signing secrets
- [ ] No broker credentials
- [ ] No Firebase config
- [ ] No paid signal data
- [ ] No private scoring or scan rules

## Webhook Receiver

- [ ] HTTPS endpoint
- [ ] Signature verification
- [ ] Timestamp replay protection
- [ ] Delivery ID duplicate protection
- [ ] 2xx response on success
- [ ] Error logging

## Automation Behavior

- [ ] Handles no-pick days
- [ ] Handles empty arrays
- [ ] Handles missing optional fields
- [ ] Handles retries
- [ ] Stores raw payload when needed

## Trading Safety

- [ ] No promise of profit
- [ ] Clear educational disclaimer
- [ ] Paper trading first for broker workflows
- [ ] Manual approval before live orders
- [ ] User controls risk and execution

## Funnel Setup

- [ ] README explains what can be built
- [ ] README links to live KamdenAI access
- [ ] Examples are easy to run
- [ ] Historical examples include assumptions
- [ ] Disclaimers are visible

# Discord Integration

Discord is a strong first use case for signal webhooks. You can create a private channel that receives formatted signal alerts automatically.

## Simple Flow

```text
KamdenAI -> Make/Zapier/custom receiver -> Discord channel
```

## Recommended Channels

- `#plan-scan`
- `#confirmed-buys`
- `#quick-exit-results`
- `#no-picks-log`

## Message Format

Example confirmed buy message:

```text
Confirmed Buy Signals - 2026-10-08

DEMOA (fictional)
Entry: $20.00
Stop: $19.50
Target: $20.50
Opening decision: Confirmed buy (rank 2)

Educational signal only. Trade at your own risk.
```

## No-Pick Message

```text
No official confirmations supplied; check review completion.
Session: 2026-10-08. No rows alone does not establish completed review.
```
